xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5041: Phone app: light mode (System / Light / Dark appearance setting)

plan.title: Phone app: light mode (System / Light / Dark appearance setting)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: About 21 files across the phone shell, one frontend hook, iOS and Android native code, docs and acceptance evidence. The native, web and docs parts are one user-visible setting and cannot ship separately without leaving a half-working Appearance control.

narratives.Problem: The Overdeck phone app (apps/mobile) is dark only. The frontend's useTheme store defaults to dark because the phone never stores 'overdeck.ui.theme', the phone skips the frontend's boot theme reconcile because it reads admin routes the phone token cannot call (PAN-4835 H-4), and the native chrome (WebView background, status bar) follows only the phone's system appearance. The operator wants light mode.
narratives.Proposal: A phone-only three-way appearance (System default, Light, Dark) stored in localStorage 'overdeck.appearance'. An inline index.html head script applies the dark class and pre-seeds the frontend's 'overdeck.ui.theme' before first paint. useTheme gains setTheme and skips its server sync in the native shell. apps/mobile/src/shell/appearance.ts holds the store and a controller that applies the resolved theme through useTheme.setTheme, sets Capacitor's built-in SystemBars style, mirrors the appearance to a new OverdeckAppearance native plugin, and follows matchMedia changes for System. Settings gets an Appearance radio group. The native plugin persists the choice (UserDefaults / SharedPreferences) and applies it at launch: iOS window overrideUserInterfaceStyle in SceneDelegate, Android AppCompatDelegate night mode before super.onCreate plus the WebView background color.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to the desktop dashboard's or browser /m page's theme behavior, storage key, default or server sync
- No System option in the desktop dashboard
- No Ledger/Broadsheet design-language choice or custom color-theme selection in the phone app
- No change to the iOS LaunchScreen.storyboard or the Android splash image
- No change to the Live Activity widget extension or the Notification Service extension
- The appearance never syncs to machines or between phones, and no machine or admin route is called
- No new npm dependency (no @capacitor/status-bar)
- Sign-out does not preserve the appearance; it resets to System

autoDecisions.summary: Store the appearance in phone localStorage 'overdeck.appearance' as the source of truth, with a native mirror used only at launch
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires phone-only storage; localStorage is the only store readable synchronously before first paint, and the native copy self-heals on every page load.

autoDecisions.summary: Drive the frontend through a new useTheme.setTheme action plus pre-seeding 'overdeck.ui.theme', and skip the theme server sync when isNativeShell() is true
autoDecisions.rationale: Smallest change that keeps the desktop identical, keeps ChatMarkdown/useColorTheme following resolvedTheme, and blocks the admin-route PUT /api/settings/ui-theme from the phone.

autoDecisions.summary: Use Capacitor 8's built-in SystemBars with explicit Light/Dark styles for the status bar
autoDecisions.rationale: No new dependency; SystemBarsStyle.Default reads the OS night mode and would ignore a Light/Dark choice.

autoDecisions.summary: Sign-out resets the appearance to System
autoDecisions.rationale: Sign-out already calls localStorage.clear(); changing signOut.ts adds scope the issue does not ask for, and the native copy self-heals after the reload.

autoDecisions.summary: Leave the iOS launch storyboard OS-drawn
autoDecisions.rationale: Only the static UIUserInterfaceStyle plist key could force it, which would break System; the no-flash requirement applies from the app's first window.

autoDecisions.summary: Android WebView background uses the exact page token colors #ffffff and #080b10
autoDecisions.rationale: The phone's import graph never loads useDesignLanguage, so no data-theme attribute is set and the :root/.dark Ledger tokens apply.

items.title: Add useTheme.setTheme and skip the theme server sync in the native shell

expected_outputs: useTheme.test.ts passes including the new setTheme and native-shell tests

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. In src/dashboard/frontend/src/hooks/useTheme.ts: import isNativeShell from '../lib/nativeShell'; make syncThemeToServer return early when isNativeShell() is true (covers the module-load sync and every action); add a setTheme(theme: 'light'|'dark') action that calls applyTheme(theme, true), stores the theme under 'overdeck.ui.theme', calls syncThemeToServer(theme), and sets { theme, resolvedTheme: theme }. Keep Theme = 'light'|'dark' and toggleTheme unchanged. Add the three tests listed in PRD WI-1 to src/dashboard/frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useTheme.test.ts using its existing module-reset pattern; the tests must not read source files.

items.title: Given an empty store, when setTheme('light') is called, then <html> no longer has the dark class, localStorage 'overdeck.ui.theme' returns 'light', and resolvedTheme is 'light'
Given globalThis.__OVERDECK_NATIVE__ = true and a mocked fetch, when the module loads with a stored theme and setTheme('dark') is called, then fetch is never called with '/api/settings/ui-theme'
Given no native flag and a mocked fetch, when setTheme('dark') is called, then fetch is called once with '/api/settings/ui-theme' and method PUT (desktop behavior preserved)
Create the phone appearance store, resolver and controller

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. Create apps/mobile/src/native/appearance.ts (OverdeckAppearance registerPlugin bridge with a no-op WebPlugin stand-in; method set({ appearance })) and apps/mobile/src/shell/appearance.ts exporting Appearance, ResolvedTheme, APPEARANCE_KEY = 'overdeck.appearance', APPEARANCES, readAppearance, writeAppearance, onAppearanceChange, useAppearance, resolveAppearance, AppearanceDeps, installAppearance and defaultAppearanceDeps exactly as specified in the PRD. installAppearance applies immediately (setTheme + setStatusBar from the resolved theme, setNative with the stored appearance), re-applies on every write, and on a matchMedia change re-runs only setTheme + setStatusBar. defaultAppearanceDeps uses useTheme.getState().setTheme, SystemBars.setStyle with SystemBarsStyle.Dark/Light (never Default), OverdeckAppearance.set with errors caught and console.warn'd, and window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'). Storage access is wrapped in try/catch like notificationPrefs.ts. Write apps/mobile/src/shell/__tests__/appearance.test.ts with the cases listed in the PRD.

items.title: Given localStorage 'overdeck.appearance' is missing or holds an invalid value, when readAppearance() runs, then it returns 'system'; and when localStorage throws, it returns 'system' without throwing
Given writeAppearance('light'), then localStorage 'overdeck.appearance' persists 'light' and a listener registered with onAppearanceChange is called once
Given stored 'light' and fake deps, when installAppearance(deps) runs, then setTheme('light'), setStatusBar('light') and setNative('light') are each called

Given stored 'system' and a fake media with matches false, when the media emits change with matches true, then setTheme('dark') is called; and given stored 'light', a media change does not call setTheme with 'dark'
Given the uninstaller returned by installAppearance is called, then the media change listener is removed and later writes do not call setTheme
Apply the appearance before first paint with an inline script in apps/mobile/index.html

verify_commands: npm --prefix apps/mobile run build && grep -c overdeck.appearance apps/mobile/dist/index.html
expected_outputs: grep prints 1 or more: the built index.html contains the boot script

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. Add the classic inline <script> from the PRD to apps/mobile/index.html <head>: it reads localStorage 'overdeck.appearance' (default 'system', try/catch), resolves with matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'), toggles the dark class on document.documentElement, and writes the resolved theme to localStorage 'overdeck.ui.theme'. Create apps/mobile/src/__tests__/appearance-boot.test.ts that reads index.html (as native-config.test.ts reads files), extracts the inline non-module script body, runs it with new Function(body)() in happy-dom with localStorage[APPEARANCE_KEY] set (import APPEARANCE_KEY from ../shell/appearance) and a stubbed window.matchMedia, and asserts the four cases in the PRD. Run npm --prefix apps/mobile run build and confirm dist/index.html keeps the script.

items.title: Given localStorage APPEARANCE_KEY = 'light' and matchMedia dark, when the index.html boot script runs, then <html> has no dark class and 'overdeck.ui.theme' is 'light'
Given APPEARANCE_KEY = 'dark' and matchMedia light, when the script runs, then <html> has the dark class and 'overdeck.ui.theme' is 'dark'
Given APPEARANCE_KEY missing and matchMedia dark, when the script runs, then <html> has the dark class (System default follows the phone)
Given npm --prefix apps/mobile run build, then apps/mobile/dist/index.html contains the 'overdeck.appearance' boot script

In apps/mobile/src/shell/SettingsScreen.tsx add props appearance: Appearance and onAppearanceChange(appearance: Appearance): void, and render the AppearanceSection from the PRD (role=radiogroup labeled 'Appearance', three role=radio buttons System/Light/Dark from APPEARANCES, aria-checked on the current one, trailing check mark, min-h-11 rows with border-b border-border, helper text) directly under the account block and before Notifications. Update every SettingsScreen render in apps/mobile/src/shell/__tests__/SettingsScreen.test.tsx to pass the new props and add the tests listed in the PRD.

items.title: Given appearance='system', when SettingsScreen renders, then a radiogroup named 'Appearance' renders three radios System, Light and Dark and only System has aria-checked='true'
Given the Settings screen, when the operator taps Light, then onAppearanceChange is called once with 'light'
Given appearance='dark', when SettingsScreen renders, then only the Dark radio has aria-checked='true'

In apps/mobile/src/shell/ShellApp.tsx add useEffect(() => installAppearance(defaultAppearanceDeps()), []) near the top of the component so it runs in every boot state, read const appearance = useAppearance(), and pass appearance and onAppearanceChange={writeAppearance} to SettingsScreen. In apps/mobile/src/shell/__tests__/ShellApp.test.tsx mock '../../native/appearance' with a spy set() and add the tests listed in the PRD, spying on globalThis.fetch to prove no '/api/settings/ui-theme' request.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6. Create apps/mobile/ios/App/App/OverdeckAppearancePlugin.swift as written in the PRD (CAPBridgedPlugin, jsName 'OverdeckAppearance', method set; UserDefaults key 'overdeck.appearance'; style(for:) maps light/dark/other to .light/.dark/.unspecified; set applies overrideUserInterfaceStyle on the bridge view controller's window on the main queue and calls setNeedsStatusBarAppearanceUpdate). In SceneDelegate.swift set window?.overrideUserInterfaceStyle = OverdeckAppearancePlugin.storedStyle() right after the UIWindow is created. In MainViewController.capacitorDidLoad register OverdeckAppearancePlugin(). Add the four project.pbxproj entries mirroring OverdeckLiveActivityPlugin.swift (PBXBuildFile in Sources, PBXFileReference, App group child, App target Sources phase) with new unique 24-hex ids; do not touch the widget or NotificationService targets. Add the string checks from the PRD to apps/mobile/src/__tests__/native-config.test.ts. Compile proof is the rig build in wi9.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. Create apps/mobile/android/app/src/main/java/ai/overdeck/app/OverdeckAppearancePlugin.java as written in the PRD (SharedPreferences file 'overdeck_appearance' key 'appearance'; nightMode maps light/dark/other to MODE_NIGHT_NO/YES/FOLLOW_SYSTEM; applyBackground sets the WebView background to 0xFFFFFFFF or 0xFF080B10 from the current uiMode; set persists, then on the UI thread calls AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode and applyBackground). In MainActivity.java register the plugin, call AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode(nightMode(stored(this))) before super.onCreate, call applyBackground after super.onCreate, and override onConfigurationChanged to re-apply the background. Keep 'uiMode' in the manifest's MainActivity configChanges. Add the PRD's string checks to native-config.test.ts. Run the PRD's Android live-System checkpoint on the emulator when available; if the page does not flip on 'adb shell cmd uimode night yes', implement the documented fallback (triggerWindowJSEvent('overdecksystemappearance') in onConfigurationChanged plus a window listener in defaultAppearanceDeps) and record the outcome for wi9.

Given AndroidManifest.xml, then the .MainActivity android:configChanges still contains uiMode, so a night-mode change does not recreate the activity
Given ./gradlew assembleDebug with JDK 21 (or the CI mobile-android job), then the build exits 0 with BUILD SUCCESSFUL

narrative.Action: PRD WI-9. Build and sync the app (npm --prefix apps/mobile run build; npm --prefix apps/mobile run cap:sync -- ios), copy to the rig per apps/mobile/README.md, create your own Simulator (never 'booted'), build with CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- (never CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO), and run steps 1-6 of PRD WI-9, saving screenshots with 'xcrun simctl io $U screenshot' as apps/mobile/acceptance/pan5041-*.png. Toggle the Simulator appearance with 'xcrun simctl ui $U appearance light|dark'. For the machine screens use a paired machine if reachable, otherwise the web build in an isolated Playwright browser with localStorage 'overdeck.appearance' = 'light' at /m. Add a '## PAN-5041 appearance' section to apps/mobile/ACCEPTANCE.md with a step table (step, evidence, result), the commit, the Simulator model, and the Android checkpoint outcome from wi7. Delete the Simulator afterwards. If the rig is unreachable, stop and tell the flywheel orchestrator with pan tell instead of marking this done.
